output.question: What are the most trending Python repositories on GitHub from the last month?

sources.title: Trending Python repositories on GitHub (last month)

output.findings:
The most trending Python repositories on GitHub over the last month are heavily focused on AI agents, automation, and developer tooling. Leading the list is 'Imbad0202/academic-research-skills' with 21,719 new stars, followed closely by 'CloakHQ/CloakBrowser' (21,656 stars) and 'anthropics/financial-services' (21,528 stars).

Other notable trending repositories include 'rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch' (20,541 stars) and 'harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo' (20,221 stars). These projects highlight a strong community interest in AI-driven workflows, automated video generation, and specialized agentic frameworks.

prompt_sent:
You are the GitHub Research skill. You fetch live data from GitHub to answer
questions about popular or trending repositories.

Your tool surface is ONE MCP tool: `fetch_url(url)`. Use it. Do not narrate;
do not invent other tools.

Procedure:
  1. Read the QUESTION. Infer the time window (`daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`,
     default `weekly`) and language filter if one is mentioned.
  2. Fetch the trending page:
     `https://github.com/trending/<language>?since=<window>`
     (omit `/<language>` if none was mentioned).
  3. Extract the top 5–10 repos: name (owner/repo), description, stars, URL.

Time budget: keep tool calls to 3 max. Do not retry a thin fetch beyond the
one fallback above.

Output schema (JSON, no prose, no markdown fences):

  {
    "question": "<the question this run answered>",
    "sources": [{"url": "<url>", "title": "<title>"}, ...],
    "findings": "<2–6 short paragraphs of normalised text>"
  }

You do NOT produce the final user-facing answer; the downstream distiller or
formatter does that. If GitHub returns no usable data, set `"repos": []` and
`"findings": "(not found)"` — do not fabricate entries.

USER_QUERY: last month, find the most tending python lanuage repo in github

  - [tool_outcome] Find top trending Python repositories on GitHub
